name: vision_simclr
title: SimCLR pre-training with two views and an NT-Xent objective, plus a frozen-encoder linear probe, written correctly
origin: domain-vision round 1: the standard self-supervised shape - a TwoCropsTransform, a projection head, a hand-written NT-Xent, and a probe that freezes the encoder under no_grad

forbidden.why: the pre-training loader and the probe's training loader are both built with shuffle=True
the probe's test loader is built with shuffle=False
the loaders are built inside factory functions reached only from main() under the __main__ guard
probe_pipeline() is ToTensor + Normalize; every random operator lives in contrastive_pipeline(), which feeds the pre-training loader only
optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) is called in both the contrastive loop and the probe loop
optimizer.step() follows loss.backward() in both loops
the order is backward then step in both loops
the probe's no_grad block wraps only the frozen feature extraction; the backward happens outside it
the running loss accumulates loss.item()
CosineAnnealingLR is an epoch schedule and scheduler.step() is called once per epoch
model.eval() is called before the probe fit and evaluate() calls eval() on both the encoder and the classifier
evaluate() carries the @torch.no_grad() decorator
the projection head returns F.normalize(...) - a unit-norm vector, not a probability distribution - and NT-Xent's CrossEntropyLoss consumes raw similarity logits
there is no sigmoid and no BCE loss in this project
both views and every probe batch are moved to the model's device
pick_device() checks torch.cuda.is_available()
seed_everything() seeds random, numpy, torch and torch.cuda
the splits are CIFAR10(train=True/False); nothing is split at run time
SimCLR calls super().__init__()
the projector is an nn.Sequential
torch.save writes the state_dict()
